arxiv-2101-09843.title: Multiple stellar populations in Asymptotic Giant Branch stars of Galactic Globular Clusters Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2101-09843.creator: E. P. Lagioia, A. P. Milone, A. F. Marino, M. Tailo, A. Renzini, M. Carlos, G. Cordoni, E. Dondoglio, S. Jang, A. Karakas, A. Dotter
arxiv-2101-09843.description: Abstract Multiple stellar populations (MPs) are a distinct characteristic of Globular Clusters (GCs). Their general properties have been widely studied among main sequence, red giant branch (RGB) and horizontal branch (HB) stars, but a common framework is still missing at later evolutionary stages.

arxiv-2107-08521.title: Non-degeneracy and quantitative stability of half-harmonic maps from ℝ \mathbb{R} to 𝕊 \mathbb{S}
arxiv-2107-08521.creator: Bin Deng, Liming Sun, Jun-cheng Wei
arxiv-2107-08521.description: Abstract . We consider half-harmonic maps from ℝ \mathbb{R} (or 𝕊 \mathbb{S} ) to 𝕊 \mathbb{S} . We prove that all (finite energy) half-harmonic maps are non-degenerate. In other words, they are integrable critical points of the energy functional. A full description of the kernel of the linearized operator around each half-harmonic map is given.

arxiv-2112-11828.title: Université Aix-Marseille Habilitation à Diriger les Recherches Quantum walks, limits and transport equations
arxiv-2112-11828.creator: Giuseppe Di Molfetta
arxiv-2112-11828.description: Abstract Abstract This manuscript gathers and subsumes a long series of works on using QW to simulate transport phenomena. Quantum Walks (QWs) consist of single and isolated quantum systems, evolving in discrete or continuous time steps according to a causal, shift-invariant unitary evolution in discrete space.

arxiv-2201-11562.title: Anyon braiding and the renormalization group
arxiv-2201-11562.creator: Alexander Stottmeister
arxiv-2201-11562.description: Abstract A braiding operation defines a real-space renormalization group for anyonic chains. The resulting renormalization group flow can be used to define a quantum scaling limit by operator-algebraic renormalization. It is illustrated how this works for the Ising chain, also known as transverse-field Ising model.

arxiv-2205-08627.title: Optimal nonparametric testing of Missing Completely At Random, and its connections to compatibility
arxiv-2205-08627.creator: Thomas B. Berrett, Richard J. Samworth
arxiv-2205-08627.description: Abstract Given a set of incomplete observations, we study the nonparametric problem of testing whether data are Missing Completely At Random (MCAR). Our first contribution is to characterise precisely the set of alternatives that can be distinguished from the MCAR null hypothesis.

arxiv-2303-08347.title: Colloquium: Gravitational Form Factors of the Proton
arxiv-2303-08347.creator: V. D. Burkert, L. Elouadrhiri, F. X. Girod, C. Lorcé, P. Schweitzer, P. E. Shanahan
arxiv-2303-08347.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by V. D. Burkert, L. Elouadrhiri, F. X. Girod, C. Lorcé, P. Schweitzer, P. E. Shanahan. The physics of the gravitational form factors of the proton, and their understanding within quantum chromodynamics, has advanced significantly in the past two decades through both theory and experiment. This Colloquium provides an overview of this progress, highlights the physical insights unveiled by studies of gravitational form factors, and reviews their interpretation in terms of the mechanical properties of the proton.

arxiv-2406-07029.title: Fairness-Aware Meta-Learning via Nash Bargaining
arxiv-2406-07029.creator: Yi Zeng, Xuelin Yang ∗, Li Chen, Cristian Canton Ferrer, Ming Jin, Michael I. Jordan, Ruoxi Jia
arxiv-2406-07029.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yi Zeng, Xuelin Yang ∗, Li Chen, Cristian Canton Ferrer, Ming Jin, Michael I. Jordan, Ruoxi Jia. To address issues of group-level fairness in machine learning, it is natural to adjust model parameters based on specific fairness objectives over a sensitive-attributed validation set. Such an adjustment procedure can be cast within a meta-learning framework. However, naive integration of fairness goals via meta-learning can cause hypergradient conflicts for subgroups, resulting in unstable convergence and compromising model performance and fairness.

arxiv-2501-08736.title: Holoview: Interactive 3D visualization of medical data in AR
arxiv-2501-08736.creator: Pankaj Kaushik, Anshul Goswami and Ojaswa Sharma
arxiv-2501-08736.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pankaj Kaushik, Anshul Goswami and Ojaswa Sharma. We introduce HoloView, an innovative augmented reality (AR) system that enhances interactive learning of human anatomical structures through immersive visualization. Combining advanced rendering techniques with intuitive gesture-based interactions, HoloView provides a comprehensive technical solution for medical education. The system architecture features a distributed rendering pipeline that offloads stereoscopic computations to a remote server, optimizing performance and enabling high-quality visualization on less powerful devices.

arxiv-2508-13643.title: Strong spectral stabilities for C 2 ​ k + 1 C_{2k+1} -free graphs
arxiv-2508-13643.creator: Lantao Zou, Yongtao Li, Yuejian Peng
arxiv-2508-13643.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lantao Zou, Yongtao Li, Yuejian Peng. The Turán-type problem for odd cycles is a classical problem in extremal graph theory. Füredi and Gunderson [Combin. 24 (4) (2015)] proved that if k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 and n ≥ 4 ​ k − 2 n\geq 4k-2 , then every n n -vertex C 2 ​ k + 1 C_{2k+1} -free graph contains at most ⌊ n 2 / 4 ⌋ \lfloor n^{2}/4\rfloor edges.

arxiv-2509-20110.title: Quantitative description of the surface tension minimum in a two-component surfactant system
arxiv-2509-20110.creator: Edgar M. Blokhuis
arxiv-2509-20110.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Edgar M. Blokhuis. The Gibbs adsorption equation is the thermodynamic cornerstone for the description and understanding of the surface tension in a surfactant solution. It relates the decrease in surface tension to an increased surfactant adsorption. In the early 1940’s, it therefore puzzled researchers to sometimes observe a minimum in the surface tension for certain surfactant solutions, which seemed to indicate surfactant desorption (even depletion) according to the Gibbs adsorption equation.

arxiv-2510-08828.title: LIV-Decoherence on Gravitational Cat States
arxiv-2510-08828.creator: Iarley P. Lobo, Kelvin Sampaio, Gislaine Varão, Moises Rojas, Valdir B. Bezerra
arxiv-2510-08828.description: Abstract Inspired by approaches based on the stochastic generalized uncertainty principle, we propose a Lindblad equation derived from the quantization of a stochastic modified dispersion relation in a Lorentz Invariance Violation (LIV) scenario. This framework enables us to investigate decoherence effects in a system of particles exhibiting gravitationally induced entanglement.

arxiv-2602-12771.title: The Configuration of Space: Probing the Way Social Interaction and Perception are Affected by Task-specific Spatial Representations in Online Video Communication
arxiv-2602-12771.creator: Yihuan CHEN, Kexue FU, Qianyi CHEN, Zhicong LU, RAY LC
arxiv-2602-12771.description: Abstract Humans live and act in 3D space, but often work and communicate on 2D surfaces. The prevalence of online communication on 2D screens raises the issue of whether human spatial configuration affects our capabilities, social perception, and behaviors when interacting with others in 2D video chat.

pmc-11712977.title: A pilot pragmatic trial of Mindfulness Based Dementia Care for care partners
pmc-11712977.creator: Leah R Hanson, Ella A Chrenka, Amanda A Herrmann, Meghan M JaKa, Michelle Barclay, Ymkje WJ Dioquino, Meghan O'Brien, Ann M Brombach, Laura Rice‐Oeschger
pmc-11712977.description: BackgroundCare partners (CPs) of people with dementia suffer from chronic stress impacting their mental and physical health. Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) has been shown to reduce depressive symptoms in CPs. Mindfulness‐Based Dementia Care (MBDC) is an adaptation of MBSR tailored to CPs.

pmc-12459787.title: Brainwide hemodynamics predict EEG neural rhythms across sleep and wakefulness in humans
pmc-12459787.creator: Leandro P. L. Jacob, Sydney M. Bailes, Stephanie D. Williams, Carsen Stringer, Laura D. Lewis
pmc-12459787.description: The brain exhibits rich oscillatory dynamics that play critical roles in vigilance and cognition, such as the neural rhythms that define sleep. These rhythms continuously fluctuate, signaling major changes in vigilance, but the widespread brain dynamics underlying these oscillations are difficult to investigate.

pmc-12483494.title: Correlation between the ultrasonographic measurement of intestinal thickening and laboratory parameters in asymptomatic dogs
pmc-12483494.creator: Iago Martins Oliveira, Sara Sueli Ferreira de Almeida, Carolle Vieira Muterlle Sprícigo, Wanessa Patrícia Rodrigues da Silva, Marco Augusto Machado Silva, Ana Flávia Machado Botelho, Danieli Brolo Martins, Naida Cristina Borges
pmc-12483494.description: Background:Intestinal ultrasound (USG) is a valuable diagnostic tool for gastrointestinal diseases in dogs. Despite its usefulness, the clinical significance of intestinal thickening in asymptomatic animals remains unclear.Aim:This study aimed to correlate the thickness of the intestinal layers with hematological and biochemical parameters in asymptomatic dogs.

pmc-12502241.title: Toxicity study of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein expressed on Bacillus subtilis spores
pmc-12502241.creator: Atiqah Hazan, Amalia A Saperi, Nurfatihah Zulkifli, Nor-Aziyah Mat Rahim, Vunjia Tiong, Hai Yen Lee, Sazaly AbuBakar
pmc-12502241.description: BackgroundThe SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is the primary antigen used in most COVID-19 vaccines. To improve protection, especially at mucosal surfaces, a robust and safe delivery system capable of inducing both systemic and mucosal immunity is needed. Bacillus subtilis spores offer a promising platform due to their stability, safety, and capacity for protein display.

pmc-12667520.title: SP3 and DEP1 Orchestrate Panicle Architecture by Jointly Regulating APO2 Expression in Rice
pmc-12667520.creator: Yuexin Liu, Niannian Chen, Xiaowei Fan, Xueqing Xia, Yilong Yao, Wen Huang, Jin Sun, Lintao Huang, Lei Wang, Hong Yu, Jiayang Li, Yongzhong Xing
pmc-12667520.description: Panicle architecture is largely determined by meristem activity. This previous study shows that DNA binding with one finger (Dof) transcription factor Short Panicle 3 (SP3) regulates panicle architecture. However, the molecular mechanisms of SP3 controlling panicle architecture remain largely unknown. Here, SP3 is shown to enhance inflorescence meristem (IM) activity.

pmc-12763992.title: Clinical outcomes after switching from omalizumab to anti-IL-5/IL-5R biologics in severe asthma: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12763992.creator: Fatma Arzu Akkuş, Fatih Çölkesen, Tuğba Önalan, Mehmet Emin Gerek, Mehmet Kılınç, Şevket Arslan
pmc-12763992.description: BackgroundSevere asthma (SA) is a heterogeneous disease composed of various clinical phenotypes, and criteria for selecting the most appropriate biological agent remain unclear. Therefore, when optimal control cannot be achieved with the initial biological therapy, switching between biological drugs is often performed.MethodsThis real-world study evaluated patients with severe asthma who initiated omalizumab treatment.

pmc-12951425.title: The detour technique: transcirculation stent coiling for complex cerebellar artery aneurysms. Illustrative cases
pmc-12951425.creator: Ahmed Altaf, Nathan Yu, Om H. Gandhi, Sami Almasri, Luis O. Tierradentro- Garcia, Linda Bagley, Omar A. Choudhri
pmc-12951425.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cerebellar artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, accounting for only 0.1%–0.3% of all intracranial aneurysms. They often present with wide necks and are usually treated with endovascular means through the vertebral arteries. Transcirculation approaches can offer ergonomic advantages when conventional anterograde endovascular approaches are technically challenging, particularly with incorporation of cerebellar artery origin from the aneurysm and less optimal stent placement angles.OBSERVATIONSThe authors present the transcirculation cases of 2 patients, a 41-year-old female with a 5- to 6-mm right superior cerebellar artery (SCA)

pmc-13301012.title: Chronic Opioid Use and Endocrine Disruption in Women: Mechanisms, Life-Course Vulnerabilities, and Reproductive Health Implications
pmc-13301012.creator: Doonyah Alucozai, Elizabeth Kwo
pmc-13301012.description: Chronic opioid use disrupts the female endocrine system, affecting the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG), hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA), and hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axes. In women, these disruptions manifest as menstrual irregularity, infertility, early menopause, reduced bone mineral density, adrenal insufficiency, and altered mood and sexual function.
